speaker: SPEAKER_00
transcript: Mr. President, it's been a long day and we thank you and we thank all the senators for their careful attention to the legal arguments and your courtesy to the managers and to the lawyers here. This has been the most bipartisan impeachment in American history and we hope it will continue to be so in the days ahead and nothing could be more bipartisan than the desire to recess. So the only issue before the Senate today, of course, is whether Donald Trump is subject to the court of impeachment that the Senate has convened. We see no need to make any further argument that this body has the power to convict. and to disqualify President Trump for his breathtaking constitutional crime of inciting a violent insurrection against our government. Tomorrow, we will address the amazing array of issues suggested by the thoughtful presentations by our colleagues, including the First Amendment, due process, partisanship under our Constitution, the Bill of Attainer Clause, and many, many more. The meantime, we waive all further arguments. We waive our 33 minutes of rebuttal, and we give those 33 minutes, gratefully, back to the Senate of the United States. All the time you're back, all the time has been yielded back.

explicit_propositions.text: This has been the most bipartisan impeachment in American history.
The only issue before the Senate today is whether Donald Trump is subject to the court of impeachment that the Senate has convened.
The Senate has the power to convict and disqualify President Trump.
President Trump committed a breathtaking constitutional crime of inciting a violent insurrection against the government.
The managers waived all further arguments.
The managers waived their 33 minutes of rebuttal.
The 33 minutes of rebuttal have been yielded back to the Senate.
All the time previously allocated to the managers has been returned to the Senate.

assumptions.text: Bipartisanship in impeachment proceedings is a desirable and meaningful goal.
The Senate’s authority to conduct impeachment trials is uncontested and self-evident.
Inciting violence against the U.S. government constitutes a clear constitutional violation.
The audience (Senate members) values efficiency and restraint in debate.
Waiving speaking time signals goodwill and commitment to procedural fairness.
The opposing side would benefit from receiving additional time, implying mutual respect.
The term 'breathtaking' conveys moral outrage that aligns with the Senate's shared norms.
